lines.t: [Title: The Watchman at the Feast]
[Jerusalem banquet: soft rejoicing, strings, hand drums]
Rise, watchman.
Stand among your brothers.
Tell of the road you walked.
Sing before this multitude.
My King, I thought I'd have a thousand words.
Now here You are...
And all I have is thanks.
Before I ever faced the thunder,
Before the watchman's trumpet cried,
You found a man who wanted heaven
With a little earth held tight.
I wanted courage without trembling,
A calling without counting cost.
You brought my hidden bargains daylight;
I wept for what I hadn't lost.
A meal to share, a wrong to settle,
A quiet yes when no one knew.
You taught these hands to serve my neighbor
Before they held a horn for You.
The breaking wasn't all destruction.
The emptying made room for trust.
I stopped rehearsing how I'd serve You
And took the next step through the dust.
Look where Your mercy brought me!
Look what Your love has done!
Jerusalem is singing—
The reign of peace begun!
Not to the horn that sounded,
Not to the feet that ran.
All glory to YahuShua—
The King who held this man!
Glory to the King!
Glory to the King!
Glory to the King!
Then came the Day I'd warned of,
And warning turned to trembling ground.
The proud still sold their false assurances;
The frightened searched as walls came down.
I heard men curse above the thunder.
I saw men kneel beside the road.
Some clenched their fists around their silver;
Some shared the little bread they owned.
The towers shook, the mighty faltered.
The schemes of violent men were tried.
And I who'd spoken of Your judgments
Had tears I could no longer hide.
No joy in watching rebels perish.
No boast that I had understood.
Your wrath was never mine for hatred.
Your holiness was wholly good.
[Instrumental: storm drums, dark brass]
Yet light broke through the dreadful hours:
A humbled heart, an opened hand,
A stranger sheltering the hunted,
A frightened brother helped to stand.
I saw how cruel a man could make it.
I saw compassion count the cost.
And in the trembling of my service,
You kept me mindful of the lost.
Not every prayer received my answer.
Not every path was clear to see.
I had no strength to claim as sovereign;
I had Your faithfulness to me.
I did not bring myself here.
I did not buy this place.
The race is finished—
But the boast is grace.
The horn lies quiet.
My hands are free.
And at Your table...
There's a place for me.
[Multitude: joyful tears; music rises into dancing]
Now Jerusalem lies before me,
No longer just a name in prayer.
The King is here among His people;
His righteous rule is everywhere.
The nations learn a different labor,
Their weapons yielded to the field.
No child must learn to praise the tyrant.
The wounds of ruined lands are healed.
And here, the bread is passed with gladness.
No elbow fights to claim the best.
The hands that once were clenched in hunger
Lie open in a place of rest.
Look where Your mercy brought us!
Look what Your love has done!
Jerusalem is singing—
The reign of peace begun!
Not to the horn that sounded,
Not to the feet that ran.
All glory to YahuShua—
Our King, the Son of Man!
[Instrumental celebration: hand drums, soaring guitar]
Each seventh day, I set my work down,
A little witness in the years.
I did not see the breadth before me;
I held the promise through my tears.
Now here unfolds the rest it pointed toward:
The seventh day, a thousand years.
The earth beneath Your just dominion,
The weary welcomed, drawing near.
No empty pause, no idle kingdom—
But holy gladness, life made right.
Our labor no more yoked to violence,
Our service flowering in delight.
Love has brought its work to harvest!
What You promised stands fulfilled!
Not because our faith was flawless—
But because Your word stands still!
Look where Your mercy brought us!
Look what Your love has done!
Jerusalem is singing—
The reign of peace begun!
The weekly rest bore witness;
Now see its meaning shine!
All glory to YahuShua—
This Kingdom, Lord, is Thine!
[Celebration: laughter, clapping, hallelujahs]
[Eight instrumental bars]
You asked me for a song, my King.
I've sung of all the road.
Let this be what they remember:
You were faithful through it all.
My race is finished.
Your glory fills my sight.
And after all that thunder...
How gentle is this light.
All glory to YahuShua.
All glory to the King.
[Strings fade; rejoicing continues]
